claims.text: The initial HEA is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi material is FCC.
The initial material consists of HEA multilayers with coherent or near-coherent interfaces.
A thin Cr-enriched interlayer can maintain lattice matching with the FCC HEA layers.
The relevant elevated-temperature creep range is approximately 500–600 °C.
Within the tested stress range, lattice diffusion and dislocation activity are both involved in creep.
A Cr-enriched interlayer will slightly modify interface coherency.
A Cr-enriched interlayer will create compositional gradients between the HEA layers.
Cr enrichment reduces lattice diffusion rates relative to a pure FCC phase.
Cr enrichment increases the barrier for dislocation nucleation.
The Cr-enriched interlayer bridges diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep by providing intermediate diffusivity and a moderate dislocation-nucleation barrier.
The dominant creep mechanism shifts from diffusion-mediated creep at low stress or temperature to dislocation-mediated creep as stress or temperature rises.
CoCrFeNiMn exhibits low- and high-stress creep regions with different stress exponents and activation energies.
Differences in stress exponent and activation energy establish a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Multilayers containing the Cr-enriched interlayer will exhibit a creep-mechanism transition distinct from multilayers without the interlayer.
Without the transition interlayer, diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep occur individually under different conditions.
An adequately thin Cr-enriched interlayer can preserve overall interface coherence without compromising the HEA chemistry.

contradictions.description: The interlayer is said to produce a distinct condition-dependent transition, but the baseline is also described as exhibiting diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep under different conditions. This makes the claimed distinction from the baseline internally unclear.
